title: A 3-year-old 50lb Goldendoodle pup named Dolly seeks a forever home after a family split-up - NewsBreak
text:
9 hours ago A loving Goldendoodle named Dolly needs a home Photo by Pet Finder/Florida Little Dog Rescue/Edited by Gary Smith A 3-year-old Goldendoodle pup is looking for a new family after her previous owners separated and could not keep her. Dolly weighs approximately 50 pounds and is available for adoption through Florida Little Dog Rescue with a $525 adoption fee.
"Dolly arrived in rescue when her previous family was splitting up, and no one could keep her," the rescue shared in her adoption details.
About This Sweet Goldendoodle
The rescue revealed that this medium-sized female Goldendoodle arrived at the rescue with matted fur that required shaving, but her coat is growing back well. Dolly is spayed, current on vaccinations, heartworm negative, microchipped, and has received a dental cleaning. She is fostered in the Flagler Beach area.
Dolly is a sweet Goldendoodle needing a home after a family separation. Photo by Pet Finder/Florida Little Dog Rescue According to her foster family, Dolly displays a calm and affectionate personality. She is house-trained and does well walking on a harness and leash. She is also crate trained, but does not need to be crated when left alone since she does not damage property. Dolly enjoys sleeping in bed with her foster family and often tries to share furniture with her humans.
How Does She Get Along With Dogs and Cats?
Have other dogs at home? No worries. Dolly gets along with dogs of all sizes and enjoys playing in the yard with other dogs.
However, she shows too much interest in cats and would do best in a home without felines unless the cat is experienced with dogs. She barks occasionally at unfamiliar people and sounds, so homes with shared walls are not recommended.
The rescue says Bruce does best in a home without cats or small children. Photo by Pet Finder/Florida Little Dog Rescue Dolly is a great Goldendoodle dog - an affectionate, calm, and gentle pooch.. Photo by Pet Finder/Florida Little Dog Rescue/Edited by Gary Smith The Goldendoodle tends to jump when greeting people and can be mouthy, behaviors her foster family is addressing. Because of her size and enthusiasm, Florida Little Dog Rescue recommends a home without small children or frail adults. She would likely do well with older, dog-savvy children.
"Dolly is a great dog - an affectionate, calm, and gentle pooch," he foster mom said. "She's a little mouthy (working on it) and is always excited to see you when you return, so she may jump to express her delight (working on that too).
"Due to her size, she would do best in a home without frail adults or small tykes, as her enthusiasm may result in a tumble. I think she would be fine with dog-savvy, older children," added her foster mom.
Interested adopters must live in Florida and can apply through the rescue's website at www.floridalittledogrescue.com , email at littledogrescue@gmail.com or call (407) 279-1127. Applications are processed in the order received. The rescue does not respond to general availability inquiries and does not adopt outside of the Sunshine State.
